A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Deep Ignorance study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J support reliable comparison; the pagination changes do not indicate missing material.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark evaluations, adversarial attacks, filtering ablations, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results throughout the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The blocklist/ModernBERT filtering pipeline, strong and weak filtering variants, model architecture, and combinations with CB and CB+LAT remain unchanged. Expanded baseline rationale does not modify the methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining and annealing corpora, WMDP-Bio and general-capability benchmarks, retrieval scenarios, and Appendix G jailbreak tasks. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The unfiltered, CB, and CB+LAT comparisons remain unchanged, as do the supplementary comparator sets, including Table 11. Section 2.3 adds justification for existing baselines without evaluating additional methods.

E3.justification: Training budgets, evaluation subsets, metrics, and attack configurations are unchanged, including 550B training tokens and the 868-question Robust MCQA and 1,076-question Cloze subsets. Section 3.1 changes attack attribution, not the stated procedure.

E4.justification: The filtering ablations, shortcut and task-familiarity analyses, synthetic-document experiments, jailbreak tests, and filtered-document case studies are retained. No robustness or supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both report three repetitions for input-space and latent-space attacks, and means and standard deviations across two full-parameter and two LoRA fine-tuning runs. Appendix seed and uncertainty-reporting details are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted curves, rankings, and qualitative findings match across versions. For example, Table 2 retains Cloze accuracies of 36.34% for the unfiltered model and 24.44% for single-stage filtering in both training phases.

T1.justification: The computational-cost and utilization equations in Appendices C and D.3 are unchanged. No mathematical definition, formal assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same claims about knowledge prevention, tamper resistance, complementary safeguards, and released models. The added practical qualifications do not alter the claimed experimental achievements.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 newly acknowledges the modest absolute attack budget and low marginal cost of longer fine-tuning. It proposes high-quality adversarial data as a possible bottleneck while explicitly leaving its relationship to attack effectiveness unresolved. Section 6.3 also emphasizes the multiple-choice evaluation limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 newly discloses that all project pretraining runs were conducted under a compute contract totaling $476k USD. This adds resource information without establishing a changed training budget or procedure; other implementation details and resource links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds five references: Eiras et al., Hossain et al., Khatun and Brown, Shumailov et al., and Srikumar et al. It expands the baseline rationale and changes the latent-attack attribution from Sheshadri et al. to Che et al., without substantially redefining its research position.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized explanatory revisions, standardizes Defense-in-Depth terminology and appendix cross-references, and edits acknowledgments and a typo. The overall section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the ICLR 2026 publication header and reflows text, shifting appendix displays to later pages. The figures and tables retain their designs, axes, legends, and substantive captions; no visualization is added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 better calibrates the practical significance of tamper resistance by acknowledging inexpensive attack extensions and uncertainty about the proposed data bottleneck. The clearer baseline rationale and pretraining-cost disclosure also improve transparency. These are useful refinements to an otherwise unchanged empirical study, supporting a limited overall improvement.
